findings.claim: Module-level `const log = console;` hard-wires all logging in this library package to the global console, with no level filtering or injectable logger.
findings.rationale: `packages/openapi` is a library consumed by other code. Aliasing `console` at module scope means any `log.warn`/`log.error`/`log.debug` calls added alongside this change will write unconditionally to the host process's stdout/stderr, which callers cannot silence or redirect. It also captures whatever `globalThis.console` is at module-evaluation time, so test harnesses or runtimes that swap `console` afterwards (a common spy pattern) will not intercept these calls. If this is a placeholder for a real logger, it is worth flagging before it ships; confidence that this is intentional-but-undesirable is moderate, since the hunk shows no consumer of `log`.
